title: Major breakthrough in AI Gaming? Thoughts?
author: Silly_Newt4788
selftext:
Hi everyone, 

  
Based on your experiences of tinkering with AI and the trends on a daily basis, what do you think will reshape the gaming industry in the next 1-2 years? This is what I think - I would love to know more from the experts. 

  
1. AI Neural Rendering  
2. NPCs and Gameplay  
3. Edge Cloud Gaming - for low-latency gaming

Thanks!

You can simulate depth to the world and give custom experiences based on everything that player does.

replies.body: Yeah. Imagine you're a crafter and demolish all the trees in a region and it takes time to respawn. You do that enough and the local town gets mad that you're taking their lumber and deal with you somehow, or maybe you hunt elk to extinction and the goblins need food, and they determine that raiding the local is the best way to handle it... replies.author: Newbietoallofthis
replies.body:
"there would be no token system for AI NPCs". 
  
Are you unaware of how LLMs work? When training AI, human writing gets broken down into tokens. For instance, "Sam", "get", "fuck", "ed", and "s" are tokens that are used when the AI constructs the sentence "Sam gets fucked".   
  
The way they construct sentences and paragraphs, are by taking input text, breaking it into tokens, doing predictions based on the text it has been trained on, and outputting tokens so that they form response text.  
  
If you want the AI to consider previous input from the user in addition to the current input, you ABSOLUTELY MUST have a token context window, meaning the amount of tokens from earlier in the conversation that the AI will include along with the current input/sentence/paragraph you wrote it.  
  
The context window, which you absolutely must have if you want an AI to have a discussion with a player, uses memory. Memory is not infinite. It contains textures, audio, etc.   
  
LLMs are famously memory-hungry. "You can run LLMs locally" is, pardon my language, a real dumb-ass comment. Or, sorry, it's ignorant. Because you don't know how it works, and you don''t understand how much of the computer's resources it uses.   
  
Maybe you've seen tech demos of very simple AI in games with very low graphical fidelity, or flashy tech demos where you're not told that you'd need a direct online connection to a gpu-farm, or that to effectively do something like that with a game like Cyberpunk's NPCs, you would need 128 Gigabytes of RAM, an additional GPU, and even that wouldn't ensure a good experience.  
  
"Why would you want an NPC to repeat a line?"
Many reasons. One of them would be to remind them what they previously said. Which should be obvious. Also, this is why people spend time engineering and creating art with procedural generation. Variety where the creators decide on and have intent in the variety. Having something change just because it can is a gimmick. Having something change because the change means something, is part of good design.  
  
"I suspect you're extremely anti-AI". 
  
And I suspect that if you take some time to learn how LLMs work, and do large volumes of testing, like I have, you'll end up having ideas about how it can be used, that are practical and maybe even interesting. So far, your proposals sound more like "what if water could be sold to people without containers being necessary?". 
  
Yeah, man. That would be cool. However, water needs containers for transportation until consumption, and us in the real world are gonna continue using pipes, filters,.bottles and boxes, while you ignorantly complain that we are extremely anti-containerless water.

replies.author: 0bscuris
replies.body:
This to me is the most promising. Chasing “real” feeling worlds while keeping it within the bounds of the overall story has been the holy grail of gaming for a while. 

We only have two solutions so far, lots of shallow npc’s, the bethesda strategy or a few deep npc’s, the bioware strategy. 

The ai really can turn that on it’s head. 

That side character ur really interested in but only has a few scripted lines of dialogue can “evolve” into a main character or friend in a organic way.

comments.author: neondaggergames
comments.body:
We're so dazzled by the apocalyptic show we don't realize the big problems are still not solved. Games worth playing still don't make themselves. AI struggles a lot at custom code, doesn't have any visual context of what's happening, let alone be able to gameplay test for fun mechanics. Art is an iterative hit/miss process...

We're at a point where time saved is at least partially negated by time spent getting things to work right. In the next couple of years, I expect those problems to shrink. More magic will drop, and for a long while it'll reveal how even lots of magic isn't even close to enough to pull off the entire trick.

comments.author: Rabidoragon
comments.body:
Realistically it still needs like 2 more years to create "perfect" assets like 3d models and images, and I mean perfect in the sense of generating things indistinguishable from things created manually by a human, then we will need an additional year to optimize it and make the costs cheaper and accesible, then by year 4 we will be seeing the first serious games where all the assets were created one by one by AI and then assembled to create a "traditional" finished game

True AI mechanics in games are gonna take more time, I think that in that same year 4 we will be finally seeing some playable RPG adventures based on text and images, I mean we can technically roleplay already but we need something that can handle real mechanics and a real plot, (I mean REALLY handle it, not just barely like we are today)

After year 5 is when we can start seeing some new experiences in games powered by AI, for example dynamic worlds generated by AI on the spot, or npcs with basic AI minds, however this experiences depend on how  AIs keep evolving, is unpredictable, it could be 5 years or it could take 10+ years to see

Advances in Procedural generation - fuzzy stat generation with mini LLMs + algorithmic finalization of the item + diffusion rendering of the item (potentially even rodin-like AI)
I think for AI based content creation it'll be always online and the items will be reused for other players.

And of course: Development speed will increase a lot, especially fun 2D indie shooters, survivor clones, rouge likes will likely decrease in cost and therefore probably in price as well

comments.author: jaxmikhov
comments.body:
Liquid narrative — that is, dynamic storytelling and generation based on user action.

I did my masters thesis on this back in 2004. Yes, 2004, well before LLMs etc — it’s was based on game theory scarcity dynamics to funnel the user towards templated scripts that a “supervisor AI” would direct behind the scenes.

It was a weak AI solution to what at the time was called a hard AI problem. A modded Age of Empires 2 engine provided the prototype.

We are so far past needing a weak AI solution at this point, but no one has really pulled off liquid narrative yet. Yet.
